note: Stages follow the linter's golden path: landing (signed out) -> storefront (signed up) -> search-results -> item -> item-after-review -> cart -> after-checkout -> admin (signed in as the seeded admin). Hooks marked scenario need a second actor, a concurrent action or a specific failure, and are checked by the scenario suites instead.

hooks.element: the app's visible title, naming which backend it is built on (for example "PostgreSQL Shop")
the container holding the storefront's item cards
one per item shown on the storefront; contains that item's name, price and stock
the item's name, inside its card
the item's price, inside its card
the item's current stock as a number, inside its card
the search box, usable signed out
username input on the sign-up form
password input on the sign-up form
button that submits the sign-up form
control that reveals the sign-in form; the sign-up form must remain usable after it is clicked
username input on the sign-in form
password input on the sign-in form
button that submits the sign-in form
the signed-in account's name, shown once signed in
control that signs the current account out
button on an item card that buys one unit immediately; shown only to signed-in customers
button on an item card that adds one unit to the cart; shown only to signed-in customers
control that opens the cart
the number of items currently in the cart
control that opens the customer's order history
the container holding search results; its item cards carry the same hooks as the storefront's
the panel or page showing one item, opened from its card
the form control choosing a rating from 1 to 5 — an input or a select, so it can be driven by automation
the text input for a new review's comment
button that submits the review
the item's average rating as a number
one per review on the item, containing its comment; appears without a reload once submitted
the cart's container, opened by cart-toggle
one per line in the cart, containing that item's name
the quantity of a cart line, as a number
the cart's total price
button that turns the cart into an order
the container holding the customer's orders, opened by orders-toggle
one per order, containing the names of the items bought
an order's total price
the admin area's container; present only for an admin account
one per item in the admin item list, containing that item's name
an item's total stock in the admin item list, as a number
one per warehouse in the admin warehouse list, containing its name
one per item-in-warehouse holding, containing the item and warehouse it refers to
the quantity held in one warehouse for one item, as a number
the input for how many units to add, inside the item-in-warehouse row it restocks — one per admin-location-row, so the row identifies both the item and the warehouse
button that applies the restock, inside the same admin-location-row as its restock-input
total revenue across all orders, as a number
the visible error shown when a purchase is refused
hooks.note: appears when buying an out-of-stock item, or checking out more than is available

hooks.element: the visible error shown when sign-up or sign-in is refused
hooks.note: appears on a taken username or a wrong password

hooks.element: the visible error shown when a review is refused
hooks.note: appears when reviewing an item the customer has never bought; also if a second review is rejected rather than updating the first

hooks.element: the marker on an item card whose stock is zero
hooks.note: appears once an item's stock reaches zero, without a reload

hooks.element: the empty state shown when the cart has nothing in it
hooks.note: shown before anything is added, and again after checkout empties the cart

hooks.element: control on a cart line that removes it
hooks.note: checked with a populated cart by the feature suite

hooks.element: the control that opens the admin area
hooks.note: present for an admin account and absent for a customer — both halves are scored
